prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2024 manifesto frames the election as a choice for change after 14 years of Conservative “chaos,” promising a mission-driven government focused on long-term national renewal for working people. It rests on three “strong foundations”: national security, secure borders, and economic stability.

Foundations and fiscal stance
- National security: Unshakeable commitment to NATO and the UK’s nuclear deterrent; a Strategic Defence Review within a year; pathway to 2.5% of GDP on defence; Martyn’s Law; tougher counter-extremism and hostile state measures.
- Secure borders: Scrap the Rwanda scheme; create a Border Security Command with counter-terror-style powers; clear the asylum backlog, end hotel use, fast-track returns, and deepen EU security cooperation.
- Economic stability: Strict fiscal rules (balance current budget; debt falling in year 5), full OBR scrutiny; no rises in National Insurance, Income Tax rates or VAT; crack down on avoidance (abolish non-dom status, close carried interest loophole, modernise HMRC).

Five missions
1) Kickstart economic growth
- Pro-business, pro-worker “securonomics” and a statutory Industrial Strategy Council.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital for ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, and green hydrogen.
- Business tax certainty: corporation tax capped at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Ten-year infrastructure plan; National Infrastructure & Service Transformation Authority.
- Rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; more bus franchising and municipal options; gigabit/5G by 2030.
- Planning reform to build 1.5m homes, new towns, “brownfield first,” targeted “grey belt” release, more social/affordable housing, leasehold reform, mortgage guarantee.
- Devolution with Local Growth Plans and multi-year council settlements.
- Immigration linked to skills plans; reduce net migration; crackdown on abuse.
- Employment: “New Deal for Working People” (ban exploitative zero-hours and fire-and-rehire; day-one rights; Single Enforcement Body; living wage remit).

2) Make Britain a clean energy superpower
- Zero-carbon electricity by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in storage, CCUS, hydrogen, marine.
- Back nuclear (extend existing plants; deliver Hinkley/Sizewell C; SMRs).
- No new North Sea exploration licences; retain existing; ban fracking and new coal.
- Strengthen windfall tax; create Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest and expand local power.
- Grid reform; British Jobs Bonus; Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes.
- Clean water enforcement; nature restoration; carbon border adjustment; green finance leadership.

3) Take back our streets
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders for antisocial behaviour; new offence protecting shopworkers.
- Knife Crime Action Plan; ban zombie knives; Young Futures hubs; new offence of criminal exploitation of children.
- Halve violence against women and girls: specialist police units and courts, better victim support, tougher standards and vetting in policing.
- More prison places; cut reoffending; probation reform; Hillsborough Law.

4) Break down barriers to opportunity
- 6,500 new teachers; free breakfast clubs in all primaries; 3,000 school-based nurseries.
- Curriculum/assessment reform; SEND inclusivity; mental health support in every school.
- Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeships Levy to a Growth & Skills Levy; HE funding reform; boost arts/sport access; football regulator.
- Tackle poverty and housing insecurity: abolish Section 21 evictions; raise standards; end feudal leasehold; homelessness strategy; review Universal Credit.

5) Build an NHS fit for the future
- Cut waiting lists with 40,000 extra weekly appointments; shared waiting lists; use independent sector capacity; workforce plan.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; accelerate innovation and clinical trials; empower patients via the NHS app.
- Primary/community care shift: more GPs; face-to-face guarantee; pharmacy prescribing; neighbourhood health centres.
- Dentistry rescue plan; National Care Service with national standards and a Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 more mental health staff; strong public health measures on smoking, vaping, junk food and energy drinks; tackle health inequalities.

Politics and foreign policy
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise Commons; immediate Lords reform (end hereditary peers, retirement age 80) and consult on replacement; votes at 16; reset with devolved governments.
- Make Brexit work: deeper EU cooperation on trade, security, and qualifications (no SM/CU/FOM return).
- Strong support for Ukraine; AUKUS; balanced China strategy; targeted trade deals; Clean Power Alliance; modernised development with a path back to 0.7% when finances allow.

All major pledges are presented as fully costed within Labour’s fiscal rules.
